resources.string: To practice, turn on Tiresias first.
Drag one finger across the screen without lifting it: Tiresias says what is under it. To activate what you hear, double-tap anywhere. For a long press, double-tap and keep your finger down.
Swipe right or left to go to the next or previous item. Swipe up or down to move by the reading control (by characters, words, headings...). These are your current gestures:

Swipe up then down, or down then up, to change the reading control: characters, words, lines, headings, links, controls, grid, windows, actions, editing, speech rate, volume... Then swipe up or down to move with that control.

Swipe down then right to open the Tiresias menu: read from top, search, the item list, describe with AI, the screen\'s text, the screen curtain and much more. A three-finger tap opens the item\'s actions.
With an edit box focused, double-tap to type. Tiresias says each letter as you type and what you delete. With the reading control on characters or words, swiping up and down moves the cursor.
If you hold both volume keys, Tiresias pauses (for example, so someone else can use the phone). Resume the same way, or by turning the screen off and on.
Four-finger triple-tap and hold: this is safe mode. It removes the screen curtain, the pause and the add-ons, and goes back to the Tiresias voice. It always works.
With the button below, Tiresias announces each gesture you make instead of performing it. To exit, tap the button again (or press Tiresias+1 on a keyboard).
Tiresias is a screen reader: it says what is on the screen and lets you control your phone with gestures, a keyboard or braille. This assistant helps you get it ready in a few steps.

If you installed Tiresias from outside a store, Android may say the accessibility setting is restricted. Open the Tiresias app info, the More options menu (top right) and “Allow restricted settings”. Then come back here.
Your Android version doesn\'t need any special permission: go on to the next step.

In Accessibility, find Tiresias, open it and turn on the switch. Android warns that Tiresias can see the screen and act on your behalf: that is what a screen reader needs. If you use another screen reader, Tiresias replaces it while it is on.
Keep the system from closing it
To save battery, some phones close services. Turn off battery optimization for Tiresias so it doesn\'t go silent.
Phones from Xiaomi, Huawei, OPPO, vivo, OnePlus and others also have an autostart or protected apps setting. Open the Tiresias app info and allow autostart and background activity.

On Samsung phones, open Settings, Battery, Background usage limits, Never sleeping apps, and add Tiresias. If Tiresias cannot install its updates, turn off Auto Blocker in Settings, Security and privacy: it blocks apps from outside the store.

On Xiaomi, Redmi and Poco phones, open the Tiresias app info and turn on Autostart; in Battery saver, choose No restrictions. Then, in Recents, touch and hold Tiresias and lock it, so HyperOS does not close it when clearing memory.

On OnePlus, OPPO and realme phones, open the Tiresias app info, Battery, and choose Do not optimise and Allow background activity. Then, in Recents, touch and hold Tiresias and choose Lock, so it is not closed when clearing memory.
On Huawei and Honor phones, open Settings, Battery, App launch, find Tiresias, turn off automatic management and leave auto-launch, secondary launch and run in background on.

On Motorola phones, if double tap fails or needs three taps, open the Moto app, Gestures, and turn off the gestures you do not use (the screen ones and the taps on the back). Also open the Tiresias app info and turn off battery saving for it.
On vivo and iQOO phones, open the Tiresias app info, Battery, and allow high background power use; also turn on autostart in Settings, Apps, Permissions.
The tutorial explains the gestures in a few minutes and has a practice area.
Tap a gesture to choose what it does. Changes apply to all apps; in Profiles you can change gestures for one app only.

Use the simple gestures? Everyday actions move to two- and three-finger taps: a two-finger double tap is Back, a two-finger triple tap is Home, a three-finger tap opens the Tiresias menu, a three-finger double tap the actions and a three-finger triple tap reads from the top; three fingers left open the notifications and right the recent apps. Angle gestures keep working.

With space and some dots at once, the braille display does a Tiresias action. Press a combination to change its action or remove it. Space with dot 7 is backspace and space with dot 8 is enter: those cannot be changed.

Screen reader for Android, in Spanish and English, without Google Play Services. Sibling of Tiresias for Windows.
The log is empty: there have been no crashes.

Tiresias, by Héctor J. Benítez Corredera. Includes eSpeak NG (GPL-3.0), SVOX Pico (Apache 2.0), ONNX Runtime (MIT), LiteRT-LM (Apache 2.0), Vosk (Apache 2.0), AndroidX and Material Components (Apache 2.0). Ideas and code adapted from TalkBack and Backtalk (Apache 2.0) and from Rescate Accesible and Lector Universal, by the same author.

Nothing on the screen is stored, logged or sent. There are no ads and no analytics. Tiresias only connects to the Internet to check for updates, download what you choose and use AI with your key when you ask for it.
